note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor) after the Recognizer became a three-way verdict (spec-bgp-update-propagation-rfc-defects N-3). RFC 7606 Section 5.4: "A BGP speaker advertising support for such a typed address family MUST handle routes with unrecognized NLRI types within that address family by discarding them, unless the relevant specification for that address family specifies otherwise." Re-read the four changed units diff by diff: mup and mvpn TestRecognizeNLRIRejectsUnimplementedTypes now compare against nlritype.Keep and nlritype.Discard exactly, which is stricter than the old bool (a recognizer answering Withdraw for an unknown type now goes red); the one moved expectation, a one-octet T1ST body, is now Withdraw (malformed implemented type) and still never Discard. The reactor fake recognizers changed only their return type through keepIf; the survivor-byte, ActionNone and BGP-LS override assertions are unchanged. All other covers and their earlier reading stand. Rejudged 2026-10-16 (independent reader) after the owner-approved multi-label withdrawal change (RFC 8277 Section 2.4, nlrisplit.LabeledWithdrawal): SynthesizeWithdraw gained an addPath bool and SynthesizeWithdrawFamilies/mpReachToUnreach an addPath predicate, which mpReachToUnreach reads only for a family nlrisplit.CarriesCompatibility names (labeled unicast, VPN). The edits in TestRFC7606Section54DropsMPUnreachOnlyUpdateRatherThanForgeEOR, TestRFC7606Section54FiltersTreatAsWithdrawSynthesis and TestRFC7606Section54FiltersWhenTheAttributeWalkIsAbandoned pass a nil addPath predicate to SynthesizeWithdrawFamilies; their families (EVPN, MVPN, MUP) carry no Compatibility field, so the predicate is never read and the discard/filter assertions are unchanged. RFC 7606 Section 5.4: "A BGP speaker advertising support for such a typed address family MUST handle routes with unrecognized NLRI types within that address family by discarding them, unless the relevant specification for that address family specifies otherwise." Verdict stands.
